summary: Russia destroyed over 10 million Ukrainian books in a July 2 attack on a publishing warehouse, while Ukrainian forces targeted Russian infrastructure including a refinery in Yaroslavl. Multiple drone and missile attacks struck Ukrainian cities including Sumy, Odesa, and Kyiv, causing casualties and infrastructure damage. Putin excluded Sheremetyevo Airport from strategic companies and ordered its main activity preserved amid ongoing aviation disruptions.
key_points: Russian forces destroyed over 10 million Ukrainian books in a July 2 attack on the BookChef publishing warehouse in Russia (Source: @UkraineNow/83232).
Ukrainian forces destroyed two Russian patrol boats and shadow fleet vessels in the Black Sea, striking targets over 1300 km from the front line (Source: @UkraineNow/83244).
Drone attacks hit Odesa and Chernihiv regions, with a cargo ship under Guinean flag catching fire after an attack (Source: @UkraineNow/83241).
Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile threat emerged from occupied Crimea (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69806).
Ukrainian drones targeted a Russian refinery in Yaroslavl, marking at least the sixth successful attack on the facility in 2026 (Source: @eRadarrua/104243).
Water supply cut off to Marganets and surrounding communities in Dnipropetrovsk region after Russian shelling damaged a pump station (Source: @UkraineNow/83248).
Ukrainian forces struck Russian targets over 700 km from the border in Yaroslavl region (Source: @UkraineNow/83244).
Drone collection drive for 7 FPV drones for GUR MOU forces in Zaporizhzhia direction ongoing (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69825).

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces escalated attacks using ballistic missiles including Iskander-M systems from Crimea and targeted critical infrastructure across Ukraine. Ukrainian forces demonstrated capability to strike deep Russian targets including refineries over 700 km from the border. Ongoing drone warfare threatens energy infrastructure and civilian areas with increasing frequency and sophistication.
sections.regional_response: International support for Ukraine continues with foreign volunteers totaling approximately 16,000 from 72 countries. US intelligence sharing with Ukraine has intensified, providing tactical advantages. Sanctions impact Russian services including Sberbank and Wildberries experiencing outages. Global food security threatened by Black Sea port blockades causing $1.05 billion in Ukrainian losses.
sections.intelligence_notes: US-Ukraine intelligence cooperation has returned to previous levels enhancing operational effectiveness. Ukrainian forces require increased anti-ballistic missile capabilities as missile attacks intensify. Russian infrastructure targeting includes energy facilities and publishing operations. Evacuation of civilians from active combat zones continues in eastern regions.
